findings.title: Public findMany API removed without caller migration
findings.body: The old InsightsBookingService exposed findMany(findManyArgs) that applied authorization plus filter conditions via Prisma findMany. This PR deletes findMany and replaces it with getBaseConditions() returning Prisma.Sql. Only the service and its test are changed, no callers are updated. Any existing production caller that still calls service.findMany() will fail at compile time or throw TypeError at runtime, breaking insights endpoints.

findings.title: Authorization SQL fragment with top-level OR is not parenthesized
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition return a fragment of the form (team condition) OR (user condition) with no outer parentheses, and getBaseConditions returns that fragment bare when there is no filter. SQL AND binds tighter than OR, so a caller composing WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <extra> gets teamCond OR (userCond AND extra) instead of (teamCond OR userCond) AND extra. Extra restrictions like date ranges or additional checks are then bypassed for one branch, returning rows that should have been excluded.

findings.title: Event-type filter OR fragment is not parenthesized
findings.body: buildFilterConditions for eventTypeId returns ("eventTypeId" = $1) OR ("eventParentId" = $1) with no outer parentheses. getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but getFilterConditions is public and returns bare OR. Any direct use as WHERE ${filter} AND <other> evaluates as A OR (B AND other) because AND has higher precedence, producing wrong filter results.

findings.title: Org scope drops individual bookings when org has no child teams
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition computes teamIds as [orgId, ...childTeamIds] but only queries memberships when teamsFromOrg.length > 0, otherwise uses empty user list. When an org has no child teams the query for orgId memberships is skipped, so the (userId = ANY(...) AND isTeamBooking=false) branch is omitted. An org owner then sees no individual bookings, only team bookings, even though org members have individual bookings that should be visible.

findings.title: Org scope test assumes deterministic order for ANY arrays
findings.body: The org-scope test asserts exact equality with Prisma.sql containing team ID array [org, team, team2, team3] and user ID array [user, user2, user3]. Those arrays come from findAllByParentId and findAllByTeamIds which have no ORDER BY, so database return order is not guaranteed. Since = ANY is order-insensitive, the implementation is correct regardless of order but the toEqual on Sql values will flake when the DB returns a different order.
